claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 show a large industrial engine with the CAT C9 ACERT label.
The report shows the physical item but no shipping or customs documentation.
The witness report explicitly states that working condition and starting were not shown.
Requires a video with audio of the engine running.
The witness report states the total number of hours operated was not shown.
Requires close-up inspection of factory seals and bolt heads for tool marks.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure or seized components.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine starting, idling, and revving.

risks.risk: High usage hours despite 'low mileage' claim.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the hour meter or a CAT ET diagnostic status report.
risks.if_unproven: as a high-hour unit requiring immediate overhaul

risks.risk: Fluid leaks or cooling system failure under pressure.
risks.proof: A video of the engine running at operating temperature showing the block and seals.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a full gasket and seal replacement

risks.proof: A screenshot of a diagnostic scan (CAT ET) showing active codes.
risks.if_unproven: as having a faulty or missing ECM

proof_requests: Video of the engine starting and running with clear audio.
Photo of the hour meter or ECM readout.
Close-up photos of the engine block bolts and cylinder head mating surfaces.
Import documentation or bill of lading from Belgium.
response.reason: The witness has positively identified the engine as a CAT C9 ACERT, allowing for a baseline valuation at the worst-case (non-running) condition.
